title: Smokey Mary train to the lakefront
summary: The train to Lake Pontchartrain, where Woodrow's and Washington Garden sat on either side of the track, took half an hour and cost fifteen cents round trip.

blocks.x: Well, no doubt. Yeah. Because I used to go to them private picnics and then I'd go to Ada Woodrow or Washington Garden and I'd dance till midnight and catch Smokey Mary. They used to call that Smokey Mary. That train used to go out there. And the camellia used to land it, which I showed you the picture of it here, alongside the wharf. So if you'd want to make a picture of that, copy it here, where you could do it.
Um, those places were right near the wharf then, Woodrow's? Yeah. That is, right at the edge of the lake. Yeah.
You see where the water started, it was not only a hundred feet away from where this dance provision would be, on both sides of life.
What was the other side, Woodrow's?

Woodrow's. Woodrow's was on this side, the east side of the railroad track, and the Washington Garden was on the west side of the old Smokey Mary track, or L&N track. Yeah. Because the L&N Railroad Company owned that track. Smokey Mary. Yeah, Smokey Mary.
How long did it take to get out there?
Oh, that'd be less than a half hour. Yeah, it didn't take at all.
It was only about a five or six mile run.

Where did you get that train then? By the river? Up there, up there near Charters in the leading field. Right up there. Charters in the leading field. How much did they charge, what was the fare out there?
I think it was fifteen cents, wasn't it? Huh? I think it was fifteen cents fare, wasn't it? Round trip ticket.
Yeah, fifteen cents for a round trip ticket.
That's only a half cent more than it costs now. Yeah.
